summary: This sermon introduces a series on silence and solitude as spiritual practices, arguing that Jesus modeled and invited his followers to regularly withdraw from busyness to lonely places for prayer. The practice positions us to hear from God and be transformed, though Western culture's emphasis on efficiency and constant distraction makes it difficult.
key_points: Jesus regularly withdrew to lonely places (eremos) to pray despite his busy ministry
Solitude is an invitation from Jesus to all followers, not extra credit for spiritual elites
Western culture's busyness and digital distraction prevent us from hearing God's whisper
Solitude means intentionally making room for God free from all inputs or agendas
Practicing solitude requires sacrificial decisions to eliminate hurry and reclaim margin
big_idea: Solitude is intentionally making room for God free from all inputs or agendas, a practice Jesus modeled and invites us into so we can hear his voice and be transformed into Christ-like love.
title: SOLITUDE: The Quiet Place
